candidates.title: Single-cell transcriptomic profiles before and after BCG vaccination with ex vivo LPS
candidates.cell_context: CD14 monocytes from three longitudinally sampled healthy donors
candidates.model_use: high-priority human single-cell domain and donor-holdout benchmark for Geneformer-compatible analyses
candidates.exclusion_reason: Longitudinal identity is donor-level; baseline and LPS-responsive transcriptomes come from different cells and do not link one cell's pre-state to its later phenotype.

candidates.title: Human macrophage trained-immunity imaging, ATAC-seq, cytometry, and code package
candidates.cell_context: primary human monocyte-derived macrophages across anonymized donors
candidates.model_use: priority benchmark for human macrophage response timing, donor variability, and post-restimulation single-cell cytokine programs
candidates.exclusion_reason: Pre-restimulation chromatin/state measurements and later single-cell cytokine measurements are not linked within the same individual cell.

candidates.title: Time-resolved monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation and innate immune memory RNA-seq
candidates.cell_context: primary human monocytes differentiated to macrophages
candidates.model_use: bulk donor-level temporal reference and negative control for claims that require single-cell identity
candidates.exclusion_reason: RNA-seq and later TNF/IL6 response are population/aliquot measurements; no same-cell molecular-to-future-response linkage exists.

candidates.title: Human monocyte trained-immunity transcriptomes before and after secondary LPS stimulation
candidates.cell_context: healthy-donor monocytes trained with inactivated SARS-CoV-2
candidates.model_use: human donor-level trained-immunity comparison with pre/post-restimulation transcriptomes
candidates.exclusion_reason: Bulk condition samples and secreted cytokines are not linked to the molecular pre-state of the same individual cell.

candidates.title: Longitudinal monocyte transcriptome, epigenome, and cytokine response after controlled malaria infection
candidates.cell_context: monocytes from five longitudinally sampled volunteers
candidates.exclusion_reason: Subject-level, not same-cell, and raw data availability is restricted by participant privacy.

candidates.title: Single-cell time series of human CD14 monocyte differentiation with M-CSF
candidates.cell_context: CD14 monocytes sampled at days 0, 3, and 6 across donors
candidates.model_use: human monocyte-to-macrophage state-space and species-compatible representation benchmark
candidates.exclusion_reason: Destructive cells are sampled at separate time points and no later inflammatory phenotype is linked to the baseline cell.

candidates.title: Multimodal human tissue macrophage profiling during ex vivo polarization
candidates.cell_context: macrophages and monocytes from multiple tissues and organ donors
candidates.model_use: strong human tissue and donor holdout benchmark for context shift and cytokine-response representations
candidates.exclusion_reason: Cultured and stimulated aliquots provide donor/tissue comparisons, not the same cell's pre-state and later phenotype.

candidates.title: Single-cell response of human CD14 monocytes to LPS with or without IL-10 signaling blockade
candidates.cell_context: human CD14 monocytes profiled after condition exposure
candidates.model_use: post-stimulation human single-cell response reference only
candidates.exclusion_reason: RNA is measured after exposure; the design cannot test whether a baseline molecular state predicts a later response.

gse94383_prefix_resolution.unresolved_detail: GEO states that cell_ids.csv maps condition and ID and separates cells into time/stimulation samples, but no authoritative source found here maps every supplementary-table prefix to a specific chip, harvest, or acquisition field. Prefixes therefore cannot support biological independence.

partner_lab_requirement.summary: An authorized study must link a human macrophage's pre-stimulation molecular state to its own later inflammatory phenotype while retaining donor, collection, stimulation, imaging, library, batch, and run lineage and independent biological units.
